042/**
043 * Provides String based properties like {@link System#getProperty(String)} for default
044 * configuration of logging levels and output. Since Rainbow Gum is configuration agnostic
045 * LogProperties is a simple string key and string value interface to allow almost any
046 * configuration implementation. The only required method to implement is
047 * {@link #valueOrNull(String)} and thus LogProperties is a functional like interface but
048 * using {@link LogProperties#builder()} is preferred so that a
049 * {@linkplain #description(String) description} can be added.
050 * <p>
051 * If a custom {@link LogProperties} is not configured the default RainbowGum uses System
052 * properties.
053 * <p>
054 * The built-in properties to configure RainbowGum are modeled after <a href=
055 * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/docs/3.1.0/reference/html/features.html#features.logging">
056 * Spring Boot logging </a>
057 * <p>
058 * LogProperties should generally be accessed with {@link #forKey(String)} (see
059 * {@link LogProperty}) which will allow safe <em>programmatic</em> data conversion of the
060 * flat key values and useful error messages to users if the property cannot be mapped or
061 * is missing. For more <em>declarative</em> injection of properties see
062 * {@link LogConfigurable} which will generate builders that can use LogProperties.
063 * <p>
064 * Rainbow Gum treats {@value #SEP} in the keys as special separator analogous to
065 * JavaScript/JSON and various other configuration systems. Furthermore to work with a
066 * wide set of configuration systems once a property key has a value it is
067 * <strong>RECOMMENDED</strong> that there should not be other property key value with a
068 * key that is a prefix of the previously mentioned key. For example allowing two
069 * properties <code>logging.example=stuff</code>, <code>logging.example.a=A</code> is not
070 * recommended as <code>logging.example</code> is defined as a leaf. The exception to this
071 * rule is keys that end with a logger name, such as levels, for consistency with Spring
072 * Boot. {@link AbstractNested} is one way for a nested format to read them.
073 * <p>
074 * Rainbow Gum out of the the box supports parsing two formats into properties:
075 * {@link Properties} text, and {@link URI#getRawQuery()} percent encoded query
076 * parameters. The two different formats have different behavior for
077 * {@link #listOrNull(String)} and {@link #mapOrNull(String)}. If a custom format of
078 * LogProperties is created those two methods may need to be extended.
079 * <p>
080 * A convention used through out Rainbow Gum is to have the property names as constants as
081 * it makes documentation easier. These constants name are suffixed with
082 * <code>_PROPERTY</code> or <code>_PREFIX</code> the former being a fully qualified key
083 * that maybe parameterized and the latter being a partial key ending with
084 * "<code>.</code>". The fully qualified keys are like leaves on a tree.
085 * <p>
086 * Property keys can be parameterized by using
087 * {@link LogProperties#interpolateKey(String, Map)} and a general pattern is
088 * <code>logging.component.{name}.prop</code> where {@value #NAME} is a parameter. Many
089 * property constants use this to allow multiple configuration of components by name.
090 *
091 * <table class="table">
092 * <caption><strong>Built-in Property Patterns</strong></caption>
093 * <tr>
094 * <th>Property Pattern</th>
095 * <th>Description</th>
096 * </tr>
097 * <tr>
098 * <td>{@value #LEVEL_PREFIX} + {@value #SEP} + logger = LEVEL</td>
099 * <td>Sets the level for the logger. If logger name is missing or is <code>root</code>
100 * then it is considered the root logger. {@link Level#INFO} is the default level for the
101 * root logger.</td>
102 * </tr>
103 * <tr>
104 * <td>{@value #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY} = {@link ChangeMode}</td>
105 * <td>Whether runtime changes are on for the configuration. Default is
106 * {@link ChangeMode#OFF}. When on, the loggers that may change are chosen with
107 * {@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX}.</td>
108 * </tr>
109 * <tr>
110 * <td>{@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} + {@value #SEP} + logger = boolean |
111 * List&lt;{@link ChangeType}&gt;</td>
112 * <td>What may change at runtime for the logger and its children. By design RainbowGum
113 * does not allow loggers to change levels once initialized. Default is none. Has no
114 * effect unless {@value #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY} is on.</td>
115 * </tr>
116 * <tr>
117 * <td>{@value #ROUTES_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
118 * <td>A comma separated list of routes that should be enabled. If not set
119 * {@value LogRouter.Router#DEFAULT_ROUTER_NAME } is the default.</td>
120 * </tr>
121 * <tr>
122 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
123 * <td>A comma separated list of appenders associated with the route. If not set
124 * {@value #APPENDERS_PROPERTY} is used.</td>
125 * </tr>
126 * <tr>
127 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY} = <code>URI</code></td>
128 * <td>Looks up a publisher by URI scheme using the {@link LogPublisherRegistry}. The
129 * publisher is then configured by the other properties starting with
130 * {@value #PUBLISHER_PREFIX}.</td>
131 * </tr>
132 * <tr>
133 * <td>{@value #PUBLISHER_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
134 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
135 * <td>Configures the route's publisher of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
136 * example <code>logging.route.default.publisher.async.bufferSize</code>. The scheme is
137 * the one written in the URI, so <code>async</code> settings apply to whichever publisher
138 * is registered as <code>async</code>.</td>
139 * </tr>
140 * <tr>
141 * <td>{@value #APPENDERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
142 * <td>A comma separated list of appenders that should be enabled. If not set
143 * {@value LogAppender#CONSOLE_APPENDER_NAME} is the default.</td>
144 * </tr>
145 * <tr>
146 * <td>{@value #APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY } = <code>URI</code></td>
147 * <td>Looks up an output by URI scheme using the {@link LogOutputRegistry}. The output is
148 * then configured by the other properties starting with {@value #OUTPUT_PREFIX}.</td>
149 * </tr>
150 * <tr>
151 * <td>{@value #APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY } = <code>URI</code></td>
152 * <td>Looks up an encoder by URI scheme using the {@link LogEncoderRegistry}. The encoder
153 * is then configured by the other properties starting with {@value #ENCODER_PREFIX}.</td>
154 * </tr>
155 * <tr>
156 * <td>{@value #OUTPUT_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
157 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
158 * <td>Configures the appender's output of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
159 * example <code>logging.appender.file.output.file.bufferSize</code>. An output built
160 * without an appender uses its own name in place of the appender's.</td>
161 * </tr>
162 * <tr>
163 * <td>{@value #ENCODER_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
164 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
165 * <td>Configures the appender's encoder of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
166 * example <code>logging.appender.console.encoder.json5.keyValues</code>. Each type has
167 * its own keys, so switching an appender's encoder leaves the other type's settings
168 * unread rather than misread. An encoder built without an appender uses its own name in
169 * place of the appender's.</td>
170 * </tr>
171 * <tr>
172 * <td>{@value #FILE_PROPERTY} = URI</td>
173 * <td>A URI or file path to log to a file. This is for Spring Boot compatibility.</td>
174 * </tr>
175 * </table>
176 *
177 * @see LogConfigurable
178 */
179public interface LogProperties {
180
181        /**
182         * properties separator.
183         */
184        static final String SEP = ".";
185
186        /**
187         * Logging properties prefix.
188         */
189        static final String ROOT_PREFIX = "logging" + SEP;
190
191        /**
192         * Controls direct fail-safe bootstrap diagnostics. {@code OFF} (also {@code false})
193         * is the default; {@code ERROR} dumps on build failure, while {@code INFO} also dumps
194         * after successful config builds. {@code ALL} (also {@code true}) additionally prints
195         * a {@link LogReporter} report after {@link RainbowGum#start()} starts the logging
196         * components. Read from system properties before properties providers run, so it
197         * remains available when loading configuration fails. The system property overrides
198         * {@link LogConfig.Builder#debug(LogConfig.DebugModeType)}.
199         */
200        static final String DEBUG_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "debug";
201
202        /**
203         * Logging level properties prefix. The value should be the name of a
204         * {@linkplain java.lang.System.Logger.Level level}.
205         */
206        static final String LEVEL_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "level";
207
208        /**
209         * Enabled level groups. The value should be a list of group names used on
210         * {@link #GROUP_PROPERTY}. This is to enable <a href=
211         * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.3.2/reference/features/logging.html#features.logging.log-groups">
212         * Spring Boot like Log Groups </a>. <em>Note that unlike Spring Boot groups are not
213         * enabled unless this property contains the group.</em>
214         */
215        static final String GROUPS_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "groups";
216
217        /**
218         * Group property with list of logger names. The level of the group is set with
219         * <code>{@value #LEVEL_PREFIX} + .{name} = Level</code> or on the router itself with
220         * <code>{@value #ROUTE_LEVEL_PREFIX} + .{name} = Level</code>. The group name can
221         * also be used in place of a logger name with {@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} and
222         * {@value #CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX}. This is largely compatible with <a href=
223         * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.3.2/reference/features/logging.html#features.logging.log-groups">
224         * Spring Boot Log Groups </a>.
225         * @see LevelResolver#parseLevel(String)
226         */
227        static final String GROUP_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "group.{name}";
228
229        /**
230         * Whether runtime changes are on: see {@link ChangeMode}.
231         */
232        static final String CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "change.mode";
233
234        /**
235         * The level threshold of events captured before Rainbow Gum is fully bound. Before
236         * Rainbow Gum is bound events are queued. By default events that are below
237         * <code>INFO</code> are not queued.
238         */
239        static final String GLOBAL_QUEUE_LEVEL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.queue.level";
240
241        /**
242         * The level threshold of queued events reported to standard error before Rainbow Gum
243         * is bound. Defaults to <code>ERROR</code>.
244         */
245        static final String GLOBAL_QUEUE_ERROR_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.queue.error";
246
247        /**
248         * Whether output uses ANSI escape codes: see {@link LogConfig.Globals.AnsiMode}.
249         * Default is {@link LogConfig.Globals.AnsiMode#AUTO}.
250         */
251        static final String GLOBAL_ANSI_MODE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.ansi.mode";
252
253        /**
254         * Which kind of lock appenders use: see {@link LogConfig.Globals.AppenderLock}.
255         * Default is {@link LogConfig.Globals.AppenderLock#AUTO}.
256         */
257        static final String GLOBAL_APPENDER_LOCK_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.appender.lock";
258
259        /**
260         * Whether the logging path may use a {@link ThreadLocal}: see
261         * {@link LogConfig.Globals.ThreadLocalMode}. Default is
262         * {@link LogConfig.Globals.ThreadLocalMode#ALLOW}.
263         */
264        static final String GLOBAL_THREAD_LOCAL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.threadLocal";
265
266        /**
267         * Opts every appender/encoder that has not been given an explicit choice into
268         * whatever this release currently believes is the best buffering/locking strategy for
269         * the platform the process is actually running on, instead of the fixed defaults
270         * ({@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}, a
271         * {@link java.nio.charset.CharsetEncoder}-based encode) used otherwise. An explicit
272         * choice - programmatic ({@code appenderType(...)}, {@code useGetBytes(...)}) or via
273         * a more specific property ({@link LogAppender#APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY}) - always wins
274         * over this property; it only ever fills in what would otherwise be unset.
275         * <p>
276         * <strong>What "best" resolves to today, and why that is not a contract:</strong>
277         * currently this only has an effect under GraalVM native-image (detected the same way
278         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#AUTO_DETECT} is - see its javadoc), where it sets
279         * the default appender type to {@code AUTO_DETECT} (this benchmark's own measurements
280         * found {@code SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} a real, repeatable win over the
281         * plain-JVM default there) and defaults text encoders to
282         * {@code String.getBytes(Charset)}-based encoding over the default
283         * {@code CharsetEncoder}-based one. On a plain JVM this property currently changes
284         * nothing at all - the measurements that motivated the native-image behavior above
285         * pointed the other way on HotSpot. None of this is a promise: as this project
286         * benchmarks more platforms, JDK versions, and encode strategies, what "optimize"
287         * resolves to on a given platform - including whether it does anything on a plain JVM
288         * at all - can and will change between releases without notice. Pin an explicit
289         * appender type/encoder strategy instead if a deployment needs a specific one to
290         * always be used.
291         */
292        static final String GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.optimize";
293
294        /**
295         * How the java.util.logging, System.Logger and JBoss Logging message style formats a
296         * message with arguments, named after the implementation that formats the same way:
297         * <ul>
298         * <li><code>jdk</code> (default, alias <code>jboss</code>):
299         * {@link java.text.MessageFormat} is used only when the message has an argument index
300         * such as <code>{0}</code>, so <code>It's done</code> is logged as is. A
301         * {@link Throwable} argument is formatted like any other argument.</li>
302         * <li><code>log4j2</code> (alias <code>logback</code>):
303         * {@link java.text.MessageFormat} is used whenever the message has arguments, so
304         * <code>It's done</code> with an argument is logged as <code>Its done</code>, because
305         * an apostrophe is a quote. A {@link Throwable} that is the last argument is
306         * formatted like any other argument and also logged with its stack trace.</li>
307         * </ul>
308         * @see LogMessageFormatter#ofJUL(LogProperties)
309         */
310        static final String MESSAGE_FORMAT_STYLE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "messageFormat.style";
311
312        /**
313         * Key values namespace, for properties that configure where an event's key values
314         * come from.
315         */
316        static final String KEY_VALUES_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "keyvalues" + SEP;
317
318        /**
319         * A comma separated list of the key value sources whose contributors add key values
320         * to events, as the lowercase names of
321         * {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source.Standard}, for example
322         * <code>defaults,slf4j</code>. When absent every source is selected, and an empty
323         * value selects none. A logging facade's own context store is always used for events
324         * logged through that facade, whether or not it is selected, and
325         * {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor#clear()} clears a store that is not
326         * selected according to
327         * {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source.Standard#clearWhenUnselected()}.
328         */
329        static final String KEY_VALUES_SOURCES_PROPERTY = KEY_VALUES_PREFIX + "sources";
330
331        /**
332         * Maximum number of alerts {@link LogAlerts} holds in its ring buffer. Read once,
333         * from whatever {@link LogProperties} {@link LogConfig.Builder#build()} has already
334         * resolved by the time it constructs {@link LogAlerts} - before any
335         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} runs.
336         * @see LogAlerts#DEFAULT_CAPACITY
337         */
338        static final String ALERTS_CAPACITY_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.capacity";
339
340        /**
341         * What {@link LogAlerts} does, once on {@link LogLifecycle#start(LogConfig) start},
342         * if it has recorded at least one error alert and still has zero
343         * {@link LogAlerts.Listener}s registered - see
344         * {@link LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction} for the three choices and
345         * {@link LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction#DUMP} for the default.
346         */
347        static final String ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.unobservedErrorsAction";
348
349        /**
350         * Alert level at which starting Rainbow Gum fails, like treating compiler warnings as
351         * errors: see {@link LogAlerts.FailLevel}. Unlike
352         * {@value #ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY} it fails whether or not a
353         * {@link LogAlerts.Listener} is registered.
354         */
355        static final String ALERTS_FAIL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.fail";
356
357        /**
358         * Alert level for property keys that were set but not read while starting: see
359         * {@link LogAlerts.UnusedKeyLevel}.
360         */
361        static final String ALERTS_UNUSED_KEY_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.unusedKey";
362
363        /**
364         * Per logger change properties prefix: see {@link ChangeType}.
365         */
366        static final String CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "change.logger";
367
368        /**
369         * Per logger caller info properties prefix: see {@link LogEvent.Caller.CallerType}.
370         * Independent of {@link #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} and {@link #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY}:
371         * resolved through its own logger-name hierarchy walk, so a value here is never
372         * overridden by a more specific {@link #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} entry or vice versa.
373         */
374        static final String CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "caller.logger";
375
376        /**
377         * Logging file property for default single file appending. The value should be a URI.
378         */
379        static final String FILE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "file.name";
380
381        /**
382         * A common key parameter is called name.
383         */
384        static final String NAME = "name";
385
386        /**
387         * For properties keys that are parameterized with {@value #NAME} the name often used
388         * if not specified is: {@value #DEFAULT_NAME}.
389         */
390        static final String DEFAULT_NAME = "default";
391
392        /**
393         * Enabled Logging appenders. The value should be a list of names. This is equivalent
394         * to {@value #ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY} with name "default".
395         */
396        static final String APPENDERS_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "appenders";
397
398        /**
399         * Logging appender prefix for configuration.
400         */
401        static final String APPENDER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "appender.{" + NAME + "}.";
402
403        /**
404         * Prefix of the properties configuring an appender's output, followed by the output's
405         * URI scheme, for example <code>logging.appender.{name}.output.file.</code>. Also
406         * used for an output built without an appender.
407         */
408        static final String OUTPUT_PREFIX = APPENDER_PREFIX + "output.";
409
410        /**
411         * Prefix of the properties configuring an appender's encoder, followed by the
412         * encoder's URI scheme, for example
413         * <code>logging.appender.{name}.encoder.json5.</code>. Also used for an encoder built
414         * without an appender.
415         */
416        static final String ENCODER_PREFIX = APPENDER_PREFIX + "encoder.";
417
418        /**
419         * Output appender property.
420         */
421        static final String APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY = OUTPUT_PREFIX + "uri";
422
423        /**
424         * Encoder appender property.
425         */
426        static final String APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY = ENCODER_PREFIX + "uri";
427
428        /**
429         * Appender flags. A list of flags (usually comma separated).
430         * @see AppenderFlag
431         */
432        static final String APPENDER_FLAGS_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_PREFIX + "flags";
433
434        /**
435         * Appender type (buffer/locking strategy). Unlike {@value #APPENDER_FLAGS_PROPERTY}
436         * this is a single value, not a list.
437         * @see LogAppender.AppenderType
438         */
439        static final String APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_PREFIX + "type";
440
441        /**
442         * Routes enabled with names comma separated.
443         */
444        static final String ROUTES_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "routes";
445
446        /**
447         * Route prefix for configuration.
448         */
449        static final String ROUTE_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "route.{" + NAME + "}.";
450
451        /**
452         * Prefix of the properties configuring a route's publisher, followed by the URI
453         * scheme of {@value #ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY}, for example
454         * <code>logging.route.{name}.publisher.async.</code>. Also used for a publisher built
455         * without a route.
456         */
457        static final String PUBLISHER_PREFIX = ROUTE_PREFIX + "publisher.";
458
459        /**
460         * Logging publisher URI property.
461         */
462        static final String ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY = PUBLISHER_PREFIX + "uri";
463
464        /**
465         * Appenders associated with a route comma separated.
466         */
467        static final String ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY = ROUTE_PREFIX + "appenders";
468
469        /**
470         * Logging level properties prefix. The value should be the name of a
471         * {@linkplain java.lang.System.Logger.Level level}.
472         */
473        static final String ROUTE_LEVEL_PREFIX = ROUTE_PREFIX + "level";
474
475        /**
476         * Route flags.
477         */
478        static final String ROUTE_FLAGS_PROPERTY = ROUTE_PREFIX + "flags";
479
480        /**
481         * Analogous to {@link System#getProperty(String)}.
482         * @param key property name.
483         * @return property value.
484         */
485        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key);
486
487        /**
488         * Analogous to {@link System#getProperty(String, String)} with the exception that the
489         * fallback cannot be null and the return cannot be null.
490         * @param key property name.
491         * @param fallback returned if the value is not found and may not be null.
492         * @return value found or fallback.
493         */
494        default String value(String key, String fallback) {
495                Objects.requireNonNull(fallback);
496                String v = valueOrNull(key);
497                if (v != null) {
498                        return v;
499                }
500                return fallback;
501        }
502
503        /**
504         * Gets a list or null if the key is missing and by default uses
505         * {@link #parseList(String)}. The default implementation will parse the string value
506         * as a list using {@link LogProperties#parseList(String)} but custom implementations
507         * may rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing
508         * configuration system.
509         * <p>
510         * The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated
511         * and percent-encoded (<a href=
512         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
513         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded</a>) for entries needing to contain the separator
514         * or an equals sign, for example: <pre><code>
515         * logging.appenders=console,file
516         * </code></pre> resolves to <code>["console", "file"]</code>, and: <pre><code>
517         * logging.appenders=one%20two,three%2Cfour
518         * </code></pre> (a space and an escaped comma) resolves to
519         * <code>["one two", "three,four"]</code>. See {@link #parseList(String)} for empty
520         * elements.
521         * @param key property name.
522         * @return list or <code>null</code>.
523         * @apiNote the reason empty list is not returned for missing key is that it creates
524         * ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.
525         */
526        default @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
527                String s = valueOrNull(key);
528                if (s == null) {
529                        return null;
530                }
531                return parseList(s);
532        }
533
534        /**
535         * Gets a map or null if the key is missing and by default uses
536         * {@link #parseMap(String)}. The default implementation will parse the string value
537         * as map using {@link LogProperties#parseMap(String)} but custom implementations may
538         * rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing configuration
539         * system.
540         * <p>
541         * The returned map must iterate in a stable order, the same every time for the same
542         * configuration, preferably the order its entries were declared.
543         * <p>
544         * The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated
545         * <code>key=value</code> pairs, percent-encoded (<a href=
546         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
547         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded</a>) for entries needing to contain the separator
548         * or an equals sign, for example: <pre><code>
549         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=environment=prod,region=us-east
550         * </code></pre> resolves to
551         * <code>{"environment": "prod", "region": "us-east"}</code>, and: <pre><code>
552         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=region=us%20east
553         * </code></pre> (a percent-encoded space) resolves to
554         * <code>{"region": "us east"}</code>.
555         * <p>
556         * When that property is not set, the map can instead be given as a list of its keys
557         * in <code>key.keys</code> and each value in <code>key.</code><em>mapKey</em>, which
558         * works with sources that only hold flat values such as system properties or
559         * environment variables, keeps the declared order, and needs no encoding: <pre><code>
560         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.keys=environment,region
561         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.environment=prod
562         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.region=us east
563         * </code></pre> A key listed without a value is an error.
564         * @param key property name.
565         * @return map or <code>null</code>.
566         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if a key listed in <code>key.keys</code> is empty
567         * or has no value.
568         * @apiNote the reason empty map is not returned for missing key is that it creates
569         * ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.
570         */
571        default @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
572                String s = valueOrNull(key);
573                if (s == null) {
574                        return PropertyMaps.fromKeys(this, key);
575                }
576                return parseMap(s);
577        }
578
579        /**
580         * Suffix of the property listing a map's keys, see {@link #mapOrNull(String)}.
581         */
582        static final String MAP_KEYS_SUFFIX = "keys";
583
584        /**
585         * Visits this properties with visitor, by default just applying visitor to this and
586         * key directly. A composite/aggregate {@link LogProperties} (one backed by more than
587         * one underlying source) overrides this to recursively visit each of its members in
588         * order, returning the first non-<code>null</code> result - which member actually
589         * produced it is exactly what visitor is handed as its first argument, so a composite
590         * never needs to know anything about what visitor is trying to build (a raw value, a
591         * resolved property, or anything else); it just walks its members and stops at the
592         * first hit.
593         * @param <R> result type.
594         * @param key property key.
595         * @param visitor applied to (the member of this properties that ends up handling the
596         * visit, key); a <code>null</code> return means keep visiting.
597         * @return first non-<code>null</code> result, or <code>null</code> if nothing visited
598         * produced one.
599         */
600        default <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key,
601                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor) {
602                return visitor.apply(this, key);
603        }
604
605        /**
606         * Searches up a {@value #SEP} separated path using this properties to check for
607         * values. The first value not missing (not <code>null</code>) will be returned.
608         * @param <T> result type
609         * @param root prefix.
610         * @param key partial key that will have prefix concated on each try of func.
611         * @param func convert function where <code>null</code> return means to keep
612         * searching.
613         * @return closest value or <code>null</code> if no value can be found.
614         * @see #findUpPathOrNull(String, Function)
615         */
616        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
617        default <T extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable T findOrNull(String root, String key,
618                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable T> func) {
619                return findUpPathOrNull(key, k -> func.apply(this, concatKey(root, k)));
620        }
621
622        /**
623         * Starts resolving a property under key against this properties - the preferred entry
624         * point for looking up and converting a property, see {@link LogProperty}.
625         * @param key key, must start with {@value #ROOT_PREFIX} and not start or end with
626         * {@value #SEP}.
627         * @return a LogProperty ready to be resolved (e.g. via
628         * {@link LogProperty#ofString()}) or given fallback keys to try (via
629         * {@link LogProperty#or(String)}).
630         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if key is malformed.
631         */
632        default LogProperty forKey(String key) {
633                return LogProperty.of(this, key);
634        }
635
636        /**
637         * Starts resolving a property under key, with a <code>{name}</code> placeholder in
638         * key interpolated to nameParam, against this properties.
639         * @param key key, containing a <code>{name}</code> placeholder, and once interpolated
640         * must start with {@value #ROOT_PREFIX} and not start or end with {@value #SEP}.
641         * @param nameParam value to interpolate for <code>{name}</code> in key.
642         * @return a LogProperty ready to be resolved (e.g. via
643         * {@link LogProperty#ofString()}) or given fallback keys to try (via
644         * {@link LogProperty#or(String, String)}).
645         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the interpolated key is malformed.
646         */
647        default LogProperty forKey(String key, String nameParam) {
648                return LogProperty.of(this, key, nameParam);
649        }
650
651        /**
652         * Describes a key and by default is usually just the key.
653         * @param key key.
654         * @return usually the key.
655         */
656        default String description(String key) {
657                return key;
658        }
659
660        /**
661         * When log properties are coalesced this method is used to resolve order. A higher
662         * number gives higher precedence.
663         * @return zero by default.
664         */
665        default int order() {
666                return 0;
667        }

669        /**
670         * Abstract log properties builder.
671         *
672         * @param <T> builder.
673         * @apiNote this abstract class can largely be ignored hence why it is sealed.
674         */
675        public sealed abstract class AbstractBuilder<T> {
676
677                /**
678                 * description
679                 */
680                protected @Nullable String description = null;
681
682                /**
683                 * order
684                 */
685                protected int order = 0;
686
687                /**
688                 * rename key
689                 */
690                protected Function<String, String> renameKey = s -> s;
691
692                /**
693                 * fallbacks
694                 */
695                protected List<LogProperties> fallbacks = new ArrayList<>();
696
697                /**
698                 * Ignored.
699                 */
700                protected AbstractBuilder() {
701                }
702
703                /**
704                 * Add a fallback properties.
705                 * @param properties fallback not null.
706                 * @return this.
707                 */
708                public T with(LogProperties properties) {
709                        this.fallbacks.add(properties);
710                        return self();
711                }
712
713                /**
714                 * For returning this.
715                 * @return this builder.
716                 */
717                protected abstract T self();
718
719                /**
720                 * Description for properties.
721                 * @param description not null.
722                 * @return this.
723                 */
724                public T description(String description) {
725                        this.description = description;
726                        return self();
727                }
728
729                /**
730                 * When log properties are coalesced this method is used to resolve order. A
731                 * higher number gives higher precedence.
732                 * @param order order.
733                 * @return this.
734                 */
735                public T order(int order) {
736                        this.order = order;
737                        return self();
738                }
739
740                /**
741                 * Renames the key before it accesses function.
742                 * @param renameKey rename key function.
743                 * @return this.
744                 */
745                public T renameKey(Function<String, String> renameKey) {
746                        this.renameKey = renameKey;
747                        return self();
748                }
749
750                /**
751                 * Removes the prefix from a key before it accesses the underlying properties.
752                 * @param prefix to be removed from start of key.
753                 * @return this.
754                 */
755                public T removeKeyPrefix(String prefix) {
756                        return renameKey(k -> LogProperties.removeKeyPrefix(k, prefix));
757                }
758
759        }

761        /**
762         * Builder for properties.
763         */
764        public final static class Builder extends AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
765
766                private @Nullable Function<Builder, LogProperties> provider = null;
767
768                private Builder() {
769                }
770
771                @Override
772                protected Builder self() {
773                        return this;
774                }
775
776                private Builder provider(Function<Builder, LogProperties> provider) {
777                        if (this.provider != null) {
778                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("from already set");
779                        }
780                        this.provider = provider;
781                        return this;
782                }
783
784                /**
785                 * Sets what is called on {@link LogProperties#valueOrNull(String)}.
786                 * @param function valueOrNull func.
787                 * @return this.
788                 */
789                public Builder fromFunction(@SuppressWarnings("exports") Function<String, @Nullable String> function) {
790                        return provider((b) -> new DefaultLogProperties(function,
791                                        Objects.requireNonNullElse(description, "function"), renameKey, order));
792                }
793
794                /**
795                 * Parses a string as {@link Properties}.
796                 * <p>
797                 * The parameter is the <strong>contents</strong> of a properties file, not a
798                 * resource, path, or file name. Passing a name such as
799                 * {@code "logging.properties"} does not load that file; it is parsed as a single
800                 * key with an empty value.
801                 * @param properties properties content as a string, for example
802                 * {@code "logging.level=INFO"}.
803                 * @return this.
804                 * @apiNote Rainbow Gum core does not read resources from the filesystem or the
805                 * classpath. If external properties are needed, it is the caller's responsibility
806                 * to read them into a string (or use a module that does, like
807                 * {@code rainbowgum-simple-props}).
808                 */
809                public Builder fromProperties(String properties) {
810                        if (description == null) {
811                                description = "PROPERTIES_STRING";
812                        }
813                        return fromFunction(PropertiesParser.readProperties(properties)::get);
814                }
815
816                /**
817                 * Parses a string as a URI query string. If the URI has no query portion then it
818                 * will be equivalent to empty properties.
819                 * @param uri percent encoded uri with separator as "<code>&amp;</code>" and key
820                 * value separator of "<code>=</code>".
821                 * @return this.
822                 */
823                public Builder fromURIQuery(URI uri) {
824                        String query = uri.getRawQuery();
825                        return provider((b) -> queryToProperties(query,
826                                        Objects.requireNonNullElse(description, "URI_QUERY(" + LogRedactor.redactUri(uri) + ")")));
827                }
828
829                private MultiMapProperties queryToProperties(@Nullable String query, String description) {
830                        Map<String, List<String>> multiMap;
831                        if (query == null) {
832                                multiMap = Map.of();
833                        }
834                        else {
835                                multiMap = parseMultiMap(query);
836                        }
837                        var properties = new MultiMapProperties(multiMap, description, renameKey, order);
838                        return properties;
839                }
840
841                /**
842                 * Builds LogProperties based on builder config.
843                 * @return this.
844                 */
845                public LogProperties build() {
846                        var f = this.provider;
847                        if (f == null) {
848                                if (!fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
849                                        return LogProperties.of(fallbacks);
850                                }
851                                throw new IllegalStateException("from was not set");
852                        }
853
854                        var first = f.apply(this);
855                        if (fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
856                                return first;
857                        }
858                        List<LogProperties> combined = new ArrayList<>();
859                        combined.add(first);
860                        combined.addAll(fallbacks);
861                        return LogProperties.of(combined);
862                }
863
864                static abstract class AbstractLogProperties implements LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
865
866                        protected final String description;
867
868                        protected final Function<String, String> renameKey;
869
870                        protected final int order;
871
872                        public AbstractLogProperties(String description, Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
873                                super();
874                                this.description = description;
875                                this.renameKey = renameKey;
876                                this.order = order;
877                        }
878
879                        @Override
880                        public int order() {
881                                return this.order;
882                        }
883
884                        @Override
885                        public String description(String key) {
886                                String rename = renameKey.apply(key);
887                                return descriptionForKey(description, rename);
888                        }
889
890                        @Override
891                        public void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
892                                out.append(description);
893                        }
894
895                        @Override
896                        public String toString() {
897                                return getClass().getSimpleName() + "[description='" + description + "', " + "order=" + order + "]";
898                        }
899
900                }
901
902                private static final class DefaultLogProperties extends AbstractLogProperties {
903
904                        private final Function<String, @Nullable String> func;
905
906                        DefaultLogProperties(Function<String, @Nullable String> func, String description,
907                                        Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
908                                super(description, renameKey, order);
909                                this.func = func;
910                        }
911
912                        @Override
913                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
914                                return func.apply(renameKey.apply(key));

921        /**
922         * Properties that can list the keys they hold, so that with
923         * {@link LogConfig.DebugModeType#HELP} (or {@link LogConfig.DebugModeType#ALL}) keys
924         * that were set but never read can be reported. A source that renames keys should
925         * name a key the way it is set in the source in {@link #description(String)}, since
926         * that is how a suggested key is reported.
927         */
928        public interface Listable extends LogProperties {
929
930                /**
931                 * The keys this source holds, as they are read (not renamed).
932                 * @return keys.
933                 */
934                Collection<String> keys();
935
936        }
937
938        /**
939         * A base for properties read from a tree of nodes, such as a TOML, HOCON or YAML
940         * document, or a configuration system that holds its settings as a tree. A subclass
941         * says how to get a named member of a node and a node's value, and this class finds
942         * the node for a key.
943         * <p>
944         * This class is only a way to implement {@link LogProperties}. Code that reads
945         * properties should depend on {@link LogProperties}, not on this class.
946         * <p>
947         * A key is split on {@value LogProperties#SEP} into member names, except that a key
948         * ending with a logger name, such as <code>logging.level.com.example</code>, ends
949         * with one member: the logger name, which can contain dots or any other character.
950         * The logger name is looked up as a single member of the node at the rest of the key
951         * (<code>logging.level</code>) and, if there is no such member, split on
952         * {@value LogProperties#SEP} like the rest of the key. The level, route level, change
953         * and caller properties end with a logger name. For example in TOML:
954         * {@snippet lang = toml :
955         * [logging.level]
956         * root = "warn"
957         * "com.example" = "debug"
958         * "com.example.sub" = "error"
959         * }
960         * The logger name <code>root</code> is the root logger, so a format that cannot have
961         * a value at <code>logging.level</code> when it has members can set the root logger's
962         * level as above.
963         * <p>
964         * {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} is called once for each lookup and nodes are not kept
965         * between lookups, so a source whose tree changes at runtime can return its current
966         * tree. Such a source should call {@link LogConfig.ChangePublisher#publish()} after a
967         * change.
968         * <p>
969         * Methods added to this class in later versions will have names starting with
970         * <code>do</code>, so a subclass should not declare methods with that prefix.
971         *
972         * @param <N> node type.
973         */
974        public static abstract class AbstractNested<N> implements LogProperties {
975
976                /**
977                 * For subclasses.
978                 */
979                protected AbstractNested() {
980                }
981
982                /**
983                 * The top node of the tree, called once for each lookup.
984                 * @return top node or <code>null</code> if there is none.
985                 */
986                protected abstract @Nullable N doRootNodeOrNull();
987
988                /**
989                 * A member of a node.
990                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or this method.
991                 * @param name member name, which is not empty and may contain
992                 * {@value LogProperties#SEP}.
993                 * @return member or <code>null</code> if the node has no member with that name.
994                 */
995                protected abstract @Nullable N doMemberNodeOrNull(N node, String name);
996
997                /**
998                 * The value of a node.
999                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or
1000                 * {@link #doMemberNodeOrNull(Object, String)}.
1001                 * @return value or <code>null</code> if the node has none, for example a node
1002                 * that only has members.
1003                 */
1004                protected abstract @Nullable String doValueNodeOrNull(N node);
1005
1006                /**
1007                 * The value of a node as a list, for a format that has lists. By default
1008                 * <code>null</code>, so {@link #listOrNull(String)} parses
1009                 * {@link #doValueNodeOrNull(Object)}.
1010                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or
1011                 * {@link #doMemberNodeOrNull(Object, String)}.
1012                 * @return list or <code>null</code> if the node is not a list.
1013                 */
1014                protected @Nullable List<String> doListNodeOrNull(N node) {
1015                        return null;
1016                }
1017
1018                /**
1019                 * The value of a node as a map, for a format that has tables of values. By
1020                 * default <code>null</code>, so {@link #mapOrNull(String)} parses
1021                 * {@link #doValueNodeOrNull(Object)} or reads the map's keys from
1022                 * <code>key.keys</code>.
1023                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or
1024                 * {@link #doMemberNodeOrNull(Object, String)}.
1025                 * @return map, iterating in a stable order, or <code>null</code> if the node is
1026                 * not a table of values.
1027                 */
1028                protected @Nullable Map<String, String> doMapNodeOrNull(N node) {
1029                        return null;
1030                }
1031
1032                @Override
1033                public final @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1034                        N node = node(key);
1035                        return node == null ? null : doValueNodeOrNull(node);
1036                }
1037
1038                @Override
1039                public final @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
1040                        N node = node(key);
1041                        if (node == null) {
1042                                return null;
1043                        }
1044                        var list = doListNodeOrNull(node);
1045                        if (list != null) {
1046                                return list;
1047                        }
1048                        String value = doValueNodeOrNull(node);
1049                        return value == null ? null : LogProperties.parseList(value);
1050                }
1051
1052                @Override
1053                public final @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
1054                        N node = node(key);
1055                        if (node != null) {
1056                                var map = doMapNodeOrNull(node);
1057                                if (map != null) {
1058                                        return map;
1059                                }
1060                                String value = doValueNodeOrNull(node);
1061                                if (value != null) {
1062                                        return LogProperties.parseMap(value);
1063                                }
1064                        }
1065                        return PropertyMaps.fromKeys(this, key);
1066                }
1067
1068                private @Nullable N node(String key) {
1069                        N root = doRootNodeOrNull();
1070                        if (root == null) {
1071                                return null;
1072                        }
1073                        var loggerKey = Loggers.Key.parseOrNull(key);
1074                        if (loggerKey == null) {
1075                                return path(root, key);
1076                        }
1077                        N prefix = path(root, loggerKey.prefix());
1078                        String loggerName = loggerKey.loggerName();
1079                        if (prefix == null || loggerName.isEmpty()) {
1080                                return prefix;
1081                        }
1082                        N member = doMemberNodeOrNull(prefix, loggerName);
1083                        return member != null ? member : path(prefix, loggerName);
1084                }
1085
1086                private @Nullable N path(N node, String path) {
1087                        N n = node;
1088                        int start = 0;
1089                        while (true) {
1090                                int end = path.indexOf(SEP, start);
1091                                String name = end < 0 ? path.substring(start) : path.substring(start, end);
1092                                if (name.isEmpty()) {
1093                                        return null;
1094                                }
1095                                N m = doMemberNodeOrNull(n, name);
1096                                if (m == null || end < 0) {
1097                                        return m;
1098                                }
1099                                n = m;
1100                                start = end + SEP.length();
1101                        }
1102                }
1103
1104        }
1105

1107         * A log properties that can be mutated like a map.
1108         */
1109        public interface MutableLogProperties extends LogProperties {
1110
1111                /**
1112                 * Assigns key to a value.
1113                 * @param key key.
1114                 * @param value value if null will remove the key.
1115                 * @return this.
1116                 */
1117                MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value);
1118
1119                /**
1120                 * Builder for MutableLogProperties.
1121                 * @return builder.
1122                 */
1123                public static Builder builder() {
1124                        return new Builder();
1125                }

1127                /**
1128                 * Mutable Log properties builder.
1129                 */
1130                public final class Builder extends AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
1131
1132                        private Map<String, String> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1133
1134                        private Builder() {
1135                        }
1136
1137                        @Override
1138                        protected Builder self() {
1139                                return this;
1140                        }
1141
1142                        /**
1143                         * Sets the backing mutable map.
1144                         * @param map backing map.
1145                         * @return this.
1146                         */
1147                        public Builder with(Map<String, String> map) {
1148                                this.map = map;
1149                                return this;
1150                        }
1151
1152                        /**
1153                         * Parses a string as {@link Properties} useful for unit testing with Java
1154                         * multiline string literal.
1155                         * @param properties properties as a string.
1156                         * @return this.
1157                         */
1158                        public Builder copyProperties(String properties) {
1159                                map.putAll(PropertiesParser.readProperties(properties));
1160                                return this;
1161                        }

1163                        /**
1164                         * Builds a mutable log properties.
1165                         * @return mutable log properties.
1166                         */
1167                        public MutableLogProperties build() {
1168                                String description = this.description;
1169                                if (description == null) {
1170                                        description = "custom mutable";
1171                                }
1172                                var first = new MapLogProperties(map, description, renameKey, order);
1173                                if (fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
1174                                        return first;
1175                                }
1176                                List<LogProperties> combined = new ArrayList<>();
1177                                combined.add(first);
1178                                combined.addAll(fallbacks);
1179                                return new CompositeMutableLogProperties(sort(combined));
1180                        }
1181
1182                        private static final class MapLogProperties extends LogProperties.Builder.AbstractLogProperties
1183                                        implements MutableLogProperties {
1184
1185                                private final Map<String, String> map;
1186
1187                                MapLogProperties(Map<String, String> map, String description, Function<String, String> renameKey,
1188                                                int order) {
1189                                        super(description, renameKey, order);
1190                                        this.map = map;
1191                                }
1192
1193                                @Override
1194                                public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1195                                        return map.get(renameKey.apply(key));
1196                                }
1197
1198                                @Override
1199                                public MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value) {
1200                                        Objects.requireNonNull(key);
1201                                        key = renameKey.apply(key);
1202                                        if (value == null) {
1203                                                map.remove(key);
1204                                                return this;
1205                                        }
1206                                        map.put(key, value);
1207                                        return this;
1208                                }
1209
1210                        }
1211
1212                }
1213
1214        }
