1224        /**
1225         * Finds global properties by checking the currently bound rainbow gum and if not set
1226         * use system properties. <strong>This method should be used sparingly and is
1227         * preferred that you get the properties through a config instance instead.</strong>
1228         * @return currently bound properties or system properties.
1229         * @apiNote the intention of this method is to be used for ServiceLoader singleton
1230         * components and other systems that maybe bound prior to rainbow gum loading that
1231         * need to determine if they should be enabled.
1232         */
1233        public static LogProperties findGlobalProperties() {
1234                return findGlobalProperties(() -> StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES);
1235        }
1236
1237        /**
1238         * Finds global properties by checking the currently bound rainbow gum and if not set
1239         * use the supplier as the fallback. <strong>This method should be used sparingly and
1240         * is preferred that you get the properties through a config instance
1241         * instead.</strong>
1242         * @param fallback supplier to use if no rainbow gum is bound.
1243         * @return currently bound properties or fallback.
1244         * @apiNote the intention of this method is to be used for ServiceLoader singleton
1245         * components and other systems that maybe bound prior to rainbow gum loading that
1246         * need to determine if they should be enabled.
1247         */
1248        public static LogProperties findGlobalProperties(Supplier<? extends LogProperties> fallback) {
1249                var gum = RainbowGum.getOrNull();
1250                if (gum != null) {
1251                        return gum.config().properties();
1252                }
1253                return Objects.requireNonNull(fallback.get());
1254        }
1255
1256        /**
1257         * Creates log properties from many log properties. Equal properties are only included
1258         * once.
1259         * @param logProperties list of properties.
1260         * @param fallback if the logProperties list is empty.
1261         * @return log properties
1262         */
1263        public static LogProperties of(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties, LogProperties fallback) {
1264                if (logProperties.isEmpty()) {
1265                        return fallback;
1266                }
1267                if (logProperties.size() == 1) {
1268                        return Objects.requireNonNull(logProperties.get(0));
1269                }
1270                var array = sort(logProperties);
1271                return new CompositeLogProperties(array);
1272        }
1273
1274        private static LogProperties[] sort(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties) {
1275                @SuppressWarnings("null") // TODO eclipse array issue
1276                LogProperties[] array = logProperties.stream()
1277                        .filter(p -> p != StandardProperties.EMPTY)
1278                        // The same source listed twice adds nothing but noise in reports and errors.
1279                        .distinct()
1280                        .toArray(size -> new LogProperties[size]);
1281                Arrays.sort(array, Comparator.comparingInt(LogProperties::order).reversed());
1282                return array;
1283        }
1284
1285        /**
1286         * Creates log properties from many log properties.
1287         * @param logProperties the list of properties.
1288         * @return if the logProperties is empty {@link StandardProperties#EMPTY} will be
1289         * used.
1290         */
1291        public static LogProperties of(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties) {
1292                return of(logProperties, StandardProperties.EMPTY);
1293        }
1294
1295        /**
1296         * Creates log properties from a URI query and provided properties. This is useful for
1297         * URI based providers where the URI query is contributing properties for the plugin.
1298         * @param uri query will be used to pull properties from using
1299         * {@link #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)}.
1300         * @param prefix part of the key that will stripped before accessing the URI
1301         * properties.
1302         * @param properties usually this is the properties coming from {@link LogConfig}.
1303         * @return combined properties where properties is tried first than the URI query
1304         * parameters.
1305         */
1306        public static LogProperties of(URI uri, String prefix, LogProperties properties) {
1307                return of(uri, prefix, properties, null);
1308        }
1309
1310        /**
1311         * Creates log properties from a URI query and provided properties. This is useful for
1312         * URI based providers where the URI query is contributing properties for the plugin.
1313         * @param uri query will be used to pull properties from using
1314         * {@link #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)}.
1315         * @param prefix part of the key that will stripped before accessing the URI
1316         * properties.
1317         * @param properties usually this is the properties coming from {@link LogConfig}.
1318         * @param uriKey where the URI came from.
1319         * @return combined properties where properties is tried first than the URI query
1320         * parameters.
1321         */
1322        public static LogProperties of(URI uri, String prefix, LogProperties properties, @Nullable String uriKey) {
1323                /*
1324                 * TODO this should be integrated with the whole providers and registries.
1325                 */
1326                String propDesc = uriKey != null ? "[" + uriKey + "]->" : "";
1327                String description = propDesc + "URI(" + LogRedactor.redactUri(uri) + ")";
1328                var uriProperties = LogProperties.builder()
1329                        .description(description)
1330                        .fromURIQuery(uri)
1331                        .renameKey(s -> LogProperties.removeKeyPrefix(s, prefix))
1332                        .build();
1333                return LogProperties.of(List.of(properties, uriProperties));
1334        }
1335
1336        /**
1337         * Parse a {@linkplain URI#getRawQuery() URI query} in <a href=
1338         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
1339         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded </a> format useful for parsing properties values
1340         * that have key values embedded in them. <strong>This parser unlike form encoding
1341         * uses <code>%20</code> for space as the data is coming from a URI.</strong>
1342         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1343         * @param consumer accept will be called for each entry and if key (left hand) does
1344         * not have a "<code>=</code>" following it the second parameter on the consumer
1345         * accept will be passed <code>null</code>.
1346         */
1347        public static void parseUriQuery(String query,
1348                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1349                parseUriQuery(query, true, consumer);
1350        }
1351
1352        /**
1353         * Parses a URI query formatted string to a Map.
1354         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1355         * @return decoded key values with last key winning over previous equal keys.
1356         * @see #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)
1357         */
1358        public static Map<String, String> parseMap(String query) {
1359                Map<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1360                parseUriQuery(query, (k, v) -> {
1361                        if (v != null) {
1362                                m.put(k, v);
1363                        }
1364                });
1365                return m;
1366        }
1367
1368        /**
1369         * Parses a URI query for a multiple value map. The list values of the map maybe empty
1370         * if the query parameter does not have any values associated with it which would be
1371         * the case if there is a parameter (key) with no "<code>=</code>" following it. For
1372         * example the following would have three entries of <code>a,b,c</code> all with empty
1373         * list: <pre>
1374         * <code>
1375         * a&amp;b&amp;c&amp;
1376         * </code> </pre>
1377         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1378         * @return decoded key values with multiple keys grouped together in order found.
1379         * @see #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)
1380         */
1381        public static Map<String, List<String>> parseMultiMap(String query) {
1382                Map<String, List<String>> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1383                BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> f = (k, v) -> {
1384                        List<String> list = Objects.requireNonNull(m.computeIfAbsent(k, _k -> new ArrayList<String>()));
1385                        if (v != null) {
1386                                list.add(v);
1387                        }
1388                };
1389                parseUriQuery(query, f);
1390                return m;
1391        }
1392
1393        /**
1394         * Parses a list of strings from a string that is <a href=
1395         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
1396         * percent encoded for escaping (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)</a> where the
1397         * separator can be either "<code>&amp;</code>" or "<code>,</code>".
1398         * <p>
1399         * An example would be using ampersand: <pre><code>
1400         *  "a&amp;b%20B&amp;c" -> ["a","b B","c"]
1401         *  </code> </pre> and comma: <pre><code>
1402         *  "a,b,c" -> ["a","b","c"]
1403         *  </code> </pre>
1404         * <p>
1405         * An element may be empty. One empty element at the start and one at the end are
1406         * dropped, so a value assembled from parts that may be missing still works
1407         * (<code>"a,"</code> and <code>",a,"</code> are <code>["a"]</code>), while every
1408         * other empty element is kept: <pre><code>
1409         *  "" -> []
1410         *  ",," -> [""]
1411         *  "a,,b" -> ["a","","b"]
1412         *  "a,," -> ["a",""]
1413         *  </code> </pre> An equals sign is part of the element: <code>"a=b"</code> is
1414         * <code>["a=b"]</code>.
1415         * @param query the comma or ampersand delimited string.
1416         * @return list of strings
1417         */
1418        public static List<String> parseList(String query) {
1419                List<String> list = new ArrayList<>();
1420                int start = 0;
1421                for (int i = 0; i < query.length(); i++) {
1422                        char c = query.charAt(i);
1423                        if (c == ',' || c == '&') {
1424                                list.add(query.substring(start, i));
1425                                start = i + 1;
1426                        }
1427                }
1428                list.add(query.substring(start));
1429                if (list.get(0).isEmpty()) {
1430                        list.remove(0);
1431                }
1432                if (!list.isEmpty() && list.get(list.size() - 1).isEmpty()) {
1433                        list.remove(list.size() - 1);
1434                }
1435                list.replaceAll(e -> PercentCodec.decode(e, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
1436                return list;
1437        }
1438
1439        private static void parseUriQuery(String query, boolean decode, BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1440                parseUriQuery(query, decode, "[&,]", consumer);
1441        }
1442
1443        private static void parseUriQuery(String query, boolean decode, String sep,
1444                        BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1445                /*
1446                 * TODO default java split has issues but is very fast
1447                 */
1448                @SuppressWarnings("StringSplitter")
1449                String[] pairs = query.split(sep);
1450                for (String pair : pairs) {
1451                        int idx = pair.indexOf("=");
1452                        String key;
1453                        String value;
1454                        if (idx == 0) {
1455                                continue;
1456                        }
1457                        else if (idx < 0) {
1458                                key = pair;
1459                                value = null;
1460                        }
1461                        else {
1462                                key = pair.substring(0, idx);
1463                                value = pair.substring(idx + 1);
1464                        }
1465                        if (decode) {
1466                                key = PercentCodec.decode(key, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1467                                if (value != null) {
1468                                        value = PercentCodec.decode(value, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1469                                }
1470
1471                        }
1472                        if (key.isBlank()) {
1473                                continue;
1474                        }
1475                        consumer.accept(key, value);
1476                }
1477        }
1478
1479        /**
1480         * Common static log properties such as System properties ane environment variables.
1481         */
1482        @CaseChanging
1483        enum StandardProperties implements LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
1484
1485                /**
1486                 * Empty properties. The order is <code>-1</code>.
1487                 */
1488                EMPTY {
1489                        @Override
1490                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1491                                return null;
1492                        }
1493
1494                        @Override
1495                        public int order() {
1496                                return -1;
1497                        }
1498                },
1499                /**
1500                 * Uses {@link System#getProperty(String)} for {@link #valueOrNull(String)}. The
1501                 * {@link #order()} is <code>400</code> which the same value as MicroProfile
1502                 * config ordinal.
1503                 */
1504                SYSTEM_PROPERTIES {
1505                        @Override
1506                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1507                                return System.getProperty(key);
1508                        }
1509
1510                        @Override
1511                        public int order() {
1512                                return 400;
1513                        }
1514                },
1515                /**
1516                 * Uses {@link System#getenv(String)} for {@link #valueOrNull(String)}.The
1517                 * {@link #order()} is <code>300</code> which is the same value as MicroProfile
1518                 * config ordinal.
1519                 */
1520                ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES {
1521                        @Override
1522                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1523                                return System.getenv(translateKey(key));
1524                        }
1525
1526                        @Override
1527                        protected String translateKey(String key) {
1528                                return key.replace(".", "_");
1529                        }
1530
1531                        @Override
1532                        public int order() {
1533                                return 300;
1534                        }
1535                };
1536
1537                @Override
1538                public String description(String key) {
1539                        String k = translateKey(key);
1540                        return name() + "[" + k + "]";
1541                }
1542
1543                /*
1544                 * Each constant's own per-constant class body (see EMPTY/SYSTEM_PROPERTIES/
1545                 * ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES above) makes getClass() an anonymous subclass with no
1546                 * canonical name, so without this LogPropertiesReporting's fallback chain would
1547                 * land on the description(dummyKey) branch instead: name() alone is a cleaner
1548                 * report for the single most common LogProperties in practice (the default when
1549                 * nothing else is configured).
1550                 */
1551                @Override
1552                public void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
1553                        out.append(name());
1554                }
1555
1556                /**
1557                 * Translate the key.
1558                 * @param key input
1559                 * @return output
1560                 */
1561                protected String translateKey(String key) {
1562                        return key;
1563                }
1564
1565        }
1566
1567        /**
1568         * Searches a {@value LogProperties#SEP} separated property path recursing up the path
1569         * till a non null value (not missing) is found.
1570         * <p>
1571         * For example assume we have a single property set like
1572         * <code>logging.level.com.stuff=DEBUG</code> and we call this function with
1573         * <code>logging.level.com.stuff.a.b</code>.
1574         * <ol>
1575         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff.a.b</code> will resolve to <code>null</code></li>
1576         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff.a</code> will resolve to <code>null</code></li>
1577         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff</code> will resolve to <code>"DEBUG"</code>, stop
1578         * and return <code>"DEBUG"</code>.</li>
1579         * </ol>
1580         * @param <T> type to return.
1581         * @param key the initial path.
1582         * @param resolveFunc function that returns the value at path or <code>null</code>.
1583         * @return value or <code>null</code> if no non null value can be found.
1584         */
1585        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
1586        public static <T extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable T findUpPathOrNull(String key,
1587                        Function<String, @Nullable T> resolveFunc) {
1588                return searchPath(key, resolveFunc, SEP);
1589        }
1590
1591        private static <T> @Nullable T searchPath(String key, Function<String, @Nullable T> resolveFunc, String sep) {
1592                String tempName = key;
1593                @Nullable T level = null;
1594                int indexOfLastDot = tempName.length();
1595                while ((level == null) && (indexOfLastDot > -1)) {
1596                        tempName = tempName.substring(0, indexOfLastDot);
1597                        level = resolveFunc.apply(tempName);
1598                        indexOfLastDot = tempName.lastIndexOf(sep);
1599                }
1600                if (level != null) {
1601                        return level;
1602                }
1603                return resolveFunc.apply("");
1604        }
1605
1606        /**
1607         * Concats a key using {@link #SEP} to the root prefix.
1608         * @param name key.
1609         * @return concat key.
1610         */
1611        static String concatKey(String name) {
1612                return concatKey(LogProperties.ROOT_PREFIX, name);
1613        }
1614
1615        /**
1616         * Concats a keys using {@link #SEP} as the separator.
1617         * @param prefix start of key.
1618         * @param name second part of key.
1619         * @return key.
1620         */
1621        static String concatKey(String prefix, String name) {
1622                if (name.equals("")) {
1623                        return prefix;
1624                }
1625                if (prefix.equals("")) {
1626                        return name;
1627                }
1628                if (prefix.endsWith(".")) {
1629                        prefix = prefix.substring(0, prefix.length() - 1);
1630                }
1631                if (name.startsWith(SEP)) {
1632                        return prefix + name;
1633                }
1634                return prefix + SEP + name;
1635        }
1636
1637        /**
1638         * Replace "{name}" tokens in property names.
1639         * @param key property name.
1640         * @param parameters tokens to replace with entry values.
1641         * @return interpolated property key.
1642         * @see #interpolateKey(String, Function)
1643         */
1644        static String interpolateKey(String key, Map<String, String> parameters) {
1645                return interpolateKey(key, parameters::get);
1646        }
1647
1648        /**
1649         * Replaces property <strong>key</strong> parameters by using the lookup function.
1650         * Property keys are often parameterized usually by some name. The parameters are
1651         * surrounded by curly braces and replaced by the lookup function. An example of the
1652         * format is <code>a.{PARAM}</code> which has a parameter named <code>PARAM</code>. If
1653         * the lookup function has <code>PARAM->b</code> then the result will be
1654         * <code>a.b</code>. If a value for a parameter is null (indicates not found) an
1655         * exception is thrown.
1656         * @param key to be interpolated.
1657         * @param lookup function that may return null for a parameter.
1658         * @return interpolated key with all parameters replaced.
1659         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the lookup function does not have a value for a
1660         * parameter.
1661         */
1662        public static String interpolateKey(String key,
1663                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") Function<String, ? extends @Nullable String> lookup)
1664                        throws IllegalArgumentException {
1665                var parameters = keyParameters(key);
1666                String result = key;
1667                for (String k : parameters) {
1668                        var v = lookup.apply(k);
1669                        if (v == null) {
1670                                throw new IllegalArgumentException(
1671                                                "Keyed parameter missing. key: '" + key + "' parameter: '" + k + "'");
1672                        }
1673                        LogProperty.Validator.validateKeyParameterValue(key, k, v);
1674                        result = result.replace("{" + k + "}", v);
1675                }
1676                return result;
1677        }
1678
1679        /**
1680         * Interpolates a named key which is a property key that has a {@value #NAME}.
1681         * @param key with name parameters.
1682         * @param name replace name token.
1683         * @return interpolated property key.
1684         */
1685        static String interpolateNamedKey(String key, String name) {
1686                return interpolateKey(key, Map.of(NAME, name));
1687        }
1688
1689        /**
1690         * Remove key prefix from the key. Prefix should end in "." but this method does not
1691         * check that.
1692         * @param key key whose prefix will be removed.
1693         * @param prefix property name prefix.
1694         * @return prefix removed if the string is prefixed.
1695         */
1696        static String removeKeyPrefix(String key, String prefix) {
1697                if (key.startsWith(prefix)) {
1698                        return key.substring(prefix.length());
1699                }
1700                return key;
1701        }
1702
1703        /**
1704         * Property prefix parameter pattern.
1705         */
1706        static final Pattern PARAMETER_PATTERN = Pattern.compile("\\{(.*?)\\}");
1707
1708        /**
1709         * Extract key parameters with {@link #PARAMETER_PATTERN}.
1710         * @param key also known as property name.
1711         * @return parameters in key.
1712         */
1713        static Set<String> keyParameters(String key) {
1714                Set<String> tokens = new LinkedHashSet<>();
1715                Matcher matcher = PARAMETER_PATTERN.matcher(key);
1716                while (matcher.find()) {
1717                        var t = matcher.group(1);
1718                        if (t == null) {
1719                                throw new IllegalStateException("bug with parameter pattern regex.");
1720                        }
1721                        tokens.add(t);
1722                }
1723                return tokens;
1724        }
1725
1726        /**
1727         * Validate key parameters.
1728         * @param key key to be interpolated with parameters.
1729         * @param parameters names of parameters which must <strong>equal</strong> the set of
1730         * the found parameters. while the order obviously does not matter the set cannot have
1731         * more parameters than found in the key.
1732         */
1733        static void validateKeyParameters(String key, Set<String> parameters) {
1734                var keyParameters = keyParameters(key);
1735                if (!parameters.equals(keyParameters)) {
1736                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Keyed parameter mismatch. key: '" + key + "' , key parameters: "
1737                                        + keyParameters + " provided parameters: " + parameters);
1738                }
1739        }
1740
1741        /**
1742         * Standard way to produce description for a key.
1743         * @param type the properties type name.
1744         * @param key the properties key translated.
1745         * @return description for key.
1746         */
1747        static String descriptionForKey(String type, String key) {
1748                return type + "[" + key + "]";
1749        }
1750
1751        /**
1752         * Standard way to produce description for a key found in a resource (a file or
1753         * similar), without a line number.
1754         * @param type the properties type name.
1755         * @param resource file like name.
1756         * @param key the properties key translated.
1757         * @return description for key.
1758         */
1759        static String descriptionForResource(String type, String resource, String key) {
1760                return type + "[" + resource + "][" + key + "]";
1761        }
1762
1763        /**
1764         * Standard way to produce description for a key found in a resource (a file or
1765         * similar) at a known index, usually a line number.
1766         * @param type the properties type name.
1767         * @param resource file like name.
1768         * @param key the properties key translated.
1769         * @param index usually line number of where key found.
1770         * @return description for key.
1771         */
1772        static String descriptionForResource(String type, String resource, String key, long index) {
1773                return type + "[" + resource + ":" + index + "][" + key + "]";
1774        }
1775
1776}
1777
1778final class MultiMapProperties extends AbstractLogProperties {
1779
1780        private final Map<String, List<String>> multiMap;
1781
1782        public MultiMapProperties(Map<String, List<String>> multiMap, String description,
1783                        Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
1784                super(description, renameKey, order);
1785                this.multiMap = multiMap;
1786        }
1787
1788        @Override
1789        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1790                return _valueOrNull(renameKey.apply(key));
1791        }
1792
1793        private @Nullable String _valueOrNull(String key) {
1794                var list = multiMap.get(key);
1795                if (list == null || list.isEmpty()) {
1796                        return null;
1797                }
1798                return list.get(0);
1799        }
1800
1801        @Override
1802        public @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
1803                return multiMap.get(renameKey.apply(key));
1804        }
1805
1806        @Override
1807        public @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
1808                String s = valueOrNull(key);
1809                if (s != null) {
1810                        return LogProperties.parseMap(s);
1811                }
1812                var map = PropertyMaps.fromKeys(this, key);
1813                if (map != null) {
1814                        return map;
1815                }
1816                /*
1817                 * Now we check for dotted notation since key was not set. key.subkey=value
1818                 */
1819                String prefix = renameKey.apply(key) + LogProperties.SEP;
1820                LinkedHashMap<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1821                for (var k : multiMap.keySet()) {
1822                        if (k.startsWith(prefix) && !k.equals(prefix)) {
1823                                String v = _valueOrNull(k);
1824                                if (v != null) {
1825                                        String _k = k.substring(prefix.length());
1826                                        m.put(_k, v);
1827                                }
1828                        }
1829                }
1830                return m.isEmpty() ? null : m;
1831        }
1832
1833}
1834
1835interface ListLogProperties extends LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
1836
1837        @Override
1838        default @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1839                for (var props : properties()) {
1840                        var value = props.valueOrNull(key);
1841                        if (value != null) {
1842                                return value;
1843                        }
1844                }
1845                return null;
1846        }
1847
1848        @Override
1849        default <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key,
1850                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor) {
1851                for (var props : properties()) {
1852                        var value = props.visit(key, visitor);
1853                        if (value != null) {
1854                                return value;
1855                        }
1856                }
1857                return null;
1858        }
1859
1860        @Override
1861        default String description(String key) {
1862                var descriptions = new ArrayList<String>();
1863                visit(key, (source, sourceKey) -> {
1864                        descriptions.add(source.description(sourceKey));
1865                        return null;
1866                });
1867                String description = String.join(", ", descriptions);
1868                if (description.length() > 120) {
1869                        return "\n    " + String.join(",\n    ", descriptions);
1870                }
1871                return description;
1872        }
1873
1874        LogProperties[] properties();
1875
1876        default StringBuilder toString(StringBuilder sb) {
1877                sb.append(getClass().getSimpleName());
1878                sb.append("[properties=").append(Arrays.deepToString(properties())).append("]");
1879                return sb;
1880        }
1881
1882        /*
1883         * Reports components separated by commas without the error description's line
1884         * wrapping (via LogPropertiesReporting.describe, the same fallback chain
1885         * LogReporter#appendGlobalProperties uses for the top level LogProperties a LogConfig
1886         * was built with) rather than per key.
1887         */
1888        @Override
1889        default void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
1890                boolean first = true;
1891                for (var p : properties()) {
1892                        if (first) {
1893                                first = false;
1894                        }
1895                        else {
1896                                out.append(", ");
1897                        }
1898                        LogPropertiesReporting.describe(out, p);
1899                }
1900        }
1901
1902}
1903
1904/*
1905 * Shared by ListLogProperties#report(Appendable) (recursively, per component) and
1906 * LogReporter's own appendGlobalProperties(Appendable, LogProperties) (for the top level
1907 * LogProperties a LogConfig was built with), so there is exactly one fallback chain for
1908 * "how do we describe an arbitrary LogProperties for a report": an explicit
1909 * Reportable#report(...) if implemented, else the concrete class' fully qualified name
1910 * (stable and free: no override needed), else, only for the rare case where the FQCN
1911 * itself is null (e.g. one of StandardProperties' own per constant enum bodies, which are
1912 * anonymous classes under the hood, before it implemented Reportable directly),
1913 * description(key) with a dummy key, since that is the only description() such a
1914 * LogProperties is guaranteed to answer at all.
1915 */
1916final class LogPropertiesReporting {
1917
1918        static final String DESCRIBE_KEY = "logging.reporter.describe";
1919
1920        private LogPropertiesReporting() {
1921        }
1922
1923        static void describe(Appendable out, LogProperties properties) throws IOException {
1924                if (properties instanceof LogReporter.Reportable r) {
1925                        r.report(out);
1926                        return;
1927                }
1928                String fqcn = properties.getClass().getCanonicalName();
1929                if (fqcn != null) {
1930                        out.append(fqcn);
1931                        return;
1932                }
1933                out.append(properties.description(DESCRIBE_KEY));
1934        }
1935
1936}
1937
1938@SuppressWarnings("ArrayRecordComponent") // TODO we did this originall because it was hot
1939                                                                                        // path but not anymore
1940record CompositeMutableLogProperties(LogProperties[] properties) implements ListLogProperties, MutableLogProperties {
1941
1942        @Override
1943        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality") // identity check to avoid self-recursion if a
1944                                                                                        // composite contains itself
1945        public MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value) {
1946                for (var p : properties()) {
1947                        if (p instanceof MutableLogProperties mp && mp != this) {
1948                                mp.put(key, value);
1949                                return this;
1950                        }
1951                }
1952                return this;
1953        }
1954
1955        @Override
1956        public String toString() {
1957                return toString(new StringBuilder()).toString();
1958        }
1959
1960}

1964record CompositeLogProperties(LogProperties[] properties) implements ListLogProperties {

1967                return toString(new StringBuilder()).toString();

1971final class PropertiesParser {
1972
1973        private PropertiesParser() {
1974        }
1975
1976        static Map<String, String> readProperties(String input) {
1977                Map<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1978                StringReader sr = new StringReader(input);
1979                try {
1980                        readProperties(sr, m::put);
1981                }
1982                catch (IOException e) {
1983                        throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
1984                }
1985                return m;
1986        }
1987
1988        static void readProperties(Reader reader, BiConsumer<String, String> consumer) throws IOException {
1989                Properties bp = prepareProperties(consumer);
1990                bp.load(reader);
1991        }
1992
1993        private static Properties prepareProperties(BiConsumer<String, String> consumer) {
1994                // Hack to use properties class to load but our map for preserved order
1995                @SuppressWarnings({ "serial", "nullness" })
1996                Properties bp = new Properties() {
1997                        @Override
1998                        @SuppressWarnings({ "nullness", "keyfor", "UnsynchronizedOverridesSynchronized" }) // checker
1999                                                                                                                                                                                                // bug
2000                        public @Nullable Object put(Object key, Object value) {
2001                                Objects.requireNonNull(key);
2002                                Objects.requireNonNull(value);
2003                                consumer.accept((String) key, (String) value);
2004                                return null;
2005                        }
2006                };
2007                return bp;
2008        }
2009
2010}
2011
2012/*
2013 * The key.keys form of LogProperties.mapOrNull, shared with implementations that override
2014 * it.
2015 */
2016final class PropertyMaps {
2017
2018        private PropertyMaps() {
2019        }
2020
2021        static @Nullable Map<String, String> fromKeys(LogProperties properties, String key) {
2022                String keysKey = key + LogProperties.SEP + LogProperties.MAP_KEYS_SUFFIX;
2023                List<String> keys = properties.listOrNull(keysKey);
2024                if (keys == null) {
2025                        return null;
2026                }
2027                Map<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
2028                for (String k : keys) {
2029                        if (k.isEmpty()) {
2030                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("'" + keysKey + "' has an empty map key");
2031                        }
2032                        String valueKey = key + LogProperties.SEP + k;
2033                        String v = properties.valueOrNull(valueKey);
2034                        if (v == null) {
2035                                throw new IllegalArgumentException(
2036                                                "map key '" + k + "' is listed in '" + keysKey + "' but '" + valueKey + "' is missing");
2037                        }
2038                        m.put(k, v);
2039                }
2040                return m;
2041        }
2042
2043}
